# Effect: eq

EQ/filter: boosts, cuts or removes one frequency band. One eq handles one band; chain several for more.

**Where to put it**: Usually first in the chain. Common uses: highpass to cut low-end mud on non-bass tracks; high_shelf to brighten; peak to fix a single frequency.

Latest parameters: `muser effects eq` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | `peak` | `lowpass` / `highpass` / `bandpass` / `notch` / `allpass` / `peak` / `low_shelf` / `high_shelf` | Filter shape. lowpass keeps what is below frequency (muffled); highpass keeps what is above (removes lows); peak boosts or cuts at frequency; low_shelf/high_shelf boost or cut all lows/highs |
| `frequency` | 1000 | 10 – 24000 Hz | Target frequency. Low 60-250; mid 250-4000; high 4000-16000 |
| `q` | 0.707 | 0.05 – 40 | Bandwidth/resonance. 0.707 gentle; 1-2 medium; >5 very narrow (for fixing spikes) |
| `gain_db` | 0 | -36 – 36 dB | Gain, only used by peak / low_shelf / high_shelf. Typically +/-2 to +/-6 |

All parameters can be omitted and take their default when omitted; when a value is out of range, `muser validate` reports the exact location.

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "eq", "shape": "high_shelf", "frequency": 8000, "gain_db": 3 }
```

## Scenario presets

- Remove low-frequency muddiness from non-bass tracks

  ```json
  {"type": "eq", "shape": "highpass", "frequency": 150, "q": 0.707}
  ```

- Brighten the highs (air)

  ```json
  {"type": "eq", "shape": "high_shelf", "frequency": 8000, "q": 0.707, "gain_db": 3}
  ```

- Make the sound dull and distant (lo-fi)

  ```json
  {"type": "eq", "shape": "lowpass", "frequency": 3500, "q": 0.707}
  ```

- Pull down the 'boxiness' of the low-mids

  ```json
  {"type": "eq", "shape": "peak", "frequency": 350, "q": 1.2, "gain_db": -4}
  ```

- Thicken the lows (kick, bass)

  ```json
  {"type": "eq", "shape": "low_shelf", "frequency": 100, "q": 0.707, "gain_db": 3}
  ```

## Tips and common mistakes

- One eq handles only one band; for several bands, chain several eq in effects.
- Cutting is safer than boosting: first cut the bands you do not need, then boost a little (within +-3dB).
- When several tracks all have energy below 100Hz they fight each other; let only the kick and bass occupy that range, and use highpass on the other tracks.
- gain_db only works for peak / low_shelf / high_shelf; writing it on a highpass raises no error but has no effect.
